name: American Samoa

findings.local_actor: AST Telecom LLC d/b/a Bluesky Communications
findings.summary: Bluesky launched a Huawei-supplied 4.5G LTE-Advanced mobile network, Huawei wireless-to-the-premise fixed broadband, online charging and VoLTE systems, upgrading its 2G/3G network across American Samoa, Samoa and the Cook Islands.

sources.publisher: FCC (AST Telecom SCRP status update, Form 5640)

findings.analyst_inference: Equipment vendor rule: Huawei supplied RAN and core, so pole prc. The launch article is a partner media release (S4); Bluesky's own FCC filing (S1) independently confirms Huawei covered equipment in its network, hence medium. still_current false: the April 2025 FCC filing reports removal and disposal complete (see ASM-002). Superseded by ASM-002 and ASM-003.

findings.local_actor: AST Telecom LLC d/b/a Bluesky Communications; US Federal Communications Commission (Secure and Trusted Communications Networks Reimbursement Program)
findings.financier: US FCC Secure and Trusted Communications Networks Reimbursement Program
findings.reversal_of: Bluesky's Huawei-supplied LTE/WTTx mobile and core network (ASM-001)
findings.summary: Under the FCC rip-and-replace programme, Bluesky removed its Huawei network equipment: FCC approved its reimbursement application in July 2022, physical replacement finished by June 2024, and destruction of the removed equipment completed in December 2024.

sources.publisher: FCC (AST Telecom SCRP status update, Form 5640)
FCC (AST Telecom SCRP status update, Form 5640)

findings.analyst_inference: Reversal reason geopolitical: the programme implements the US Secure Networks Act's national-security exclusion of Huawei/ZTE. Samoa News (S3) reports an FCC-approved cost estimate above $49.9m and prorated allocation above $19.75m; values left null because these are approval figures relayed second-hand and the filings opened state no funds received. The April 2025 filing says software, optimisation and VoLTE work continue and cites a funding shortfall.

findings.local_actor: AST Telecom LLC d/b/a Bluesky Communications
findings.summary: Bluesky switched on an Ericsson-built network in American Samoa: Ericsson Radio System plus cloud core, unified data management and IMS, supporting 3G, 4G and non-standalone 5G. The upgrade began in 2022 and replaced Huawei equipment.

sources.publisher: FCC (AST Telecom SCRP status update, Form 5640)

findings.analyst_inference: Equipment vendor rule: Ericsson supplies RAN and core, so pole third. Corroboration rests on Ericsson's release plus Bluesky's separate FCC filing naming Ericsson as replacement vendor; Mobile World Live largely echoes Ericsson. Neither Ericsson source mentions Huawei; the replacement link comes from the FCC filing. Tier 5: FCC April 2025 filing reports physical replacement complete by June 2024.

findings.local_actor: American Samoa Telecommunications Authority (ASTCA, owns the American Samoa branch); Hawaiki Submarine Cable LP (system owner, New Zealand)
findings.summary: The ASTCA-owned American Samoa branch of the TE SubCom-built Hawaiki trans-Pacific cable landed at Tafuna in April 2018, linking the territory to Hawaii, the US West Coast, Australia and New Zealand; planned cost close to $30 million.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment vendor rule: TE SubCom manufactured the cable, so pole us; supplier attribution comes from Computerworld only. Announced value is the governor's 'close to $30 million' planned cost, treated as approximate. Samoa News notes ASG Employees Retirement Fund support, but its financing role is not specified, so financier null. Pre-2020; in use per 2020 SubTel report, not reconfirmed for 2026.

facilities.null_reason: one search found only a generic ocean data-centre feature datelined Pago Pago and a call-centre plan; a 2022 DOI-hosted ASTCA proposal to relocate the cable landing station into a data-centre-grade building had no confirmed progress
